span.label: **TWO LITERATURES STUDYING ONE THING AT DIFFERENT DOSES, AND THE DOSE IS WHY THEY NEVER MET:** students of memory investigate `one or two stimulus exposures`; students of attention investigate `several hundred`. Memory calls it repetition priming; attention calls it automaticity. `Quotation withheld.` **The fourth record today about one name covering two things - and the first running the other way**: forster-davis1984, tulving1990 and was2019 each SPLIT a term the field used as one, and Logan JOINS two the field used as separate
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE CLAIM IS MADE FALSIFIABLE BEFORE IT IS TESTED, BY NAMING THREE PROPERTIES THAT WOULD HAVE TO MATCH:** `The main empirical question asked in this article is whether automaticity and repetition priming share three characteristics: (1) POWER-FUNCTION SPEED-UP ... (2) ITEM SPECIFICITY ... (3) ASSOCIATIVE BASIS.` Each is then phrased as a question - `Quotation withheld?` **Three named tests, stated before the experiments, any one of which could have killed the claim.** Same discipline as Schmidt2009's rapid-chase criteria (Q-811), and rare enough in this corpus to be worth counting
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE MECHANISM IS A STORAGE CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY ITEM-SPECIFICITY IS A PREDICTION AND NOT A FINDING:** the common mechanism is `Quotation withheld.` If what is stored is a record of each encounter with a particular item, then benefit MUST be specific to that item - the second characteristic falls out of the theory rather than being observed alongside it. **A theory that predicts one of its own tests is stronger than one that accommodates it**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE BRIDGE IS THE POINT, STATED AS THE ARTICLE'S PURPOSE:** `Quotation withheld.` **A paper whose contribution is a connection rather than a result** - and for this corpus that is the interesting kind, because a citation graph shows that two literatures do not cite each other and cannot show that they should

span.note: differs in: THE PAPER MARKS THE PARAMETER WITH `IN THAT`. The span: 'The instance theory DIFFERS FROM the logogen model (Morton, 1969, 1979) and the familiarity model (Balota & Chumbley, 1984) IN THAT IT PREDICTS AN ASSOCIATIVE BASIS FOR REPETITION PRIMING AND AUTOMATICITY WHEREAS THOSE MODELS DO N[OT].' The disagreement turns on whether repetition priming has an associative basis - stated, quotable, and absent from the edge until now. Q-437.

span.label: repetition priming —part-of→ automaticity
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — **`THE FIRST FEW STEPS ON THE WAY TO` IS A CONTINUUM CLAIM AND `part-of` IS THE CLOSEST THE VOCABULARY COMES.** It is not that priming is a component of automaticity - it is the same process earlier on. `same-as` would overstate (they differ in degree and in everything that follows from degree); `is-a` is wrong; **there is no `earlier-stage-of` and this is the fifth thing today the enforced vocabulary cannot say** (Q-804, Q-806, Q-812, Q-822). Weight 0.9 and `Theoretically` is inside the quote - this is the article's thesis, and the three characteristics are the test of it.
